017package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp.auth;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.AssertionUtils.*;
020
021import java.io.*;
022import java.net.*;
023import java.nio.charset.*;
024import java.time.*;
025import java.util.concurrent.*;
026
027import com.sun.net.httpserver.*;
028
029/**
030 * A minimal loopback ({@code http://127.0.0.1}) HTTP listener that captures the single authorization-code redirect an
031 * IdP sends back to a native/CLI OAuth client (SEP-837 loopback redirect handling).
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * Binds to the loopback interface &mdash; by default on an ephemeral port (the RFC 8252 &sect;7.3 port-agnostic strategy),
035 * or on a caller-chosen <em>fixed</em> port (the "bind-first" strategy) when constructed via
036 * {@link #LoopbackRedirectReceiver(String, int, String)} &mdash; so the effective redirect URI (see
037 * {@link #redirectUri()}) is only reachable from the same host.  The first request to the callback path completes
038 * {@link #awaitCallback(Duration)} with the full request URI (including the {@code code}/{@code state}/{@code iss} query
039 * parameters); the browser receives a small "you may close this window" page.
040 *
041 * <p>
042 * Use with try-with-resources so the underlying server is always stopped.
043 *
044 * @since 10.0.0
045 */
046public class LoopbackRedirectReceiver implements AutoCloseable {
047
048   private static final String DEFAULT_PATH = "/callback";
049   private static final String DEFAULT_HTML =
050      "<html><body><h3>Authorization received</h3><p>You may close this window and return to the application.</p></body></html>";
051
052   private final HttpServer server;
053   private final String path;
054   private final int port;
055   private final String host;
056   private final CompletableFuture<URI> callback = new CompletableFuture<>();
057
058   /**
059    * Opens a receiver on an ephemeral loopback port using the default callback path {@code /callback}.
060    *
061    * @return A started receiver.
062    * @throws IOException If the loopback server could not be started.
063    */
064   @SuppressWarnings("resource") // factory hands the started receiver (and its bound socket) to the caller, who must close it (see class javadoc).
065   public static LoopbackRedirectReceiver open() throws IOException {
066      return new LoopbackRedirectReceiver(DEFAULT_PATH, DEFAULT_HTML);
067   }
068
069   /**
070    * Opens a receiver on an ephemeral loopback port (the port-agnostic strategy, RFC 8252 &sect;7.3).
071    *
072    * @param path The callback path (must start with {@code /}).  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or blank.
073    * @param successHtml The HTML body returned to the browser on the callback.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
074    * @throws IOException If the loopback server could not be started.
075    */
076   public LoopbackRedirectReceiver(String path, String successHtml) throws IOException {
077      this(path, 0, successHtml);
078   }
079
080   /**
081    * Opens a receiver on a caller-chosen <em>fixed</em> loopback port (the "bind-first" strategy for strict
082    * exact-match authorization servers that reject port-agnostic loopback redirects).
083    *
084    * <p>
085    * Pass {@code port == 0} for an ephemeral port (identical to {@link #LoopbackRedirectReceiver(String, String)}); a
086    * non-zero port binds exactly that port so it matches a {@link LoopbackRedirectUris#forPort(int, String) forPort}
087    * registration.  A fixed port can fail to bind if already in use &mdash; the {@link IOException} surfaces that to the
088    * caller.
089    *
090    * @param path The callback path (must start with {@code /}).  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or blank.
091    * @param bindPort The fixed loopback port to bind, or {@code 0} for an ephemeral port.  Must not be negative.
092    * @param successHtml The HTML body returned to the browser on the callback.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
093    * @throws IOException If the loopback server could not be started (e.g. the fixed port is already in use).
094    */
095   public LoopbackRedirectReceiver(String path, int bindPort, String successHtml) throws IOException {
096      this.path = assertArgNotNullOrBlank("path", path);
097      assertArg(path.startsWith("/"), "path must start with '/' (was '%s')", path);
098      assertArg(bindPort >= 0, "port must not be negative (was %s)", bindPort);
099      assertArgNotNull("successHtml", successHtml);
100      var html = successHtml.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
101      var svr = HttpServer.create(new InetSocketAddress(InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress(), bindPort), 0);
102      try {
103         port = svr.getAddress().getPort();
104         host = hostLiteral(svr.getAddress().getAddress());
105         svr.createContext(path, ex -> {
106            var full = URI.create("http://" + host + ":" + port + ex.getRequestURI().toString());
107            callback.complete(full);
108            ex.getResponseHeaders().add("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8");
109            ex.sendResponseHeaders(200, html.length);
110            try (var os = ex.getResponseBody()) {
111               os.write(html);
112            }
113         });
114         svr.start();
115      } catch (RuntimeException e) { // HTT: createContext()/start() on a freshly-created HttpServer registered with exactly one already-validated ('/'-prefixed) path never throws in practice; not reproducible without mocking/subclassing the JDK's sealed com.sun.net.httpserver implementation
116         svr.stop(0);  // HTT: only reachable if the try-block above throws; see catch line above -- don't leak the bound socket if wiring fails after create()
117         throw e; // HTT: only reachable if the try-block above throws; see catch line above
118      }
119      server = svr;
120   }
121
122   /** Formats the bound loopback address as a URI host literal, bracketing IPv6 (e.g. {@code [::1]}). */
123   private static String hostLiteral(InetAddress addr) {
124      var ip = addr.getHostAddress();
125      var pct = ip.indexOf('%');  // strip any IPv6 zone/scope id
126      if (pct >= 0) // HTT: addr is always InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress() (see the sole call site above), which resolves to an IPv4 loopback address with no '%' zone-id suffix on this JVM/OS's network stack -- environment-dependent, unreachable here without a differently-configured host
127         ip = ip.substring(0, pct); // HTT: only reachable if the zone-id is present; see the 'if' line above
128      return addr instanceof Inet6Address ? "[" + ip + "]" : ip; // HTT: addr is always an IPv4 Inet4Address in this environment (see rationale above), so the Inet6Address bracketing arm is unreachable here
129   }
130
131   /**
132    * Returns the loopback redirect URI the IdP should redirect the user-agent back to.
133    *
134    * @return The redirect URI (e.g. {@code http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback}).
135    */
136   public URI redirectUri() {
137      return URI.create("http://" + host + ":" + port + path);
138   }
139
140   /**
141    * Returns the ephemeral loopback port the receiver is listening on.
142    *
143    * @return The port.
144    */
145   public int port() {
146      return port;
147   }
148
149   /**
150    * Blocks until the IdP redirects to the callback path, or the timeout elapses.
151    *
152    * @param timeout The maximum time to wait.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
153    * @return The full callback request URI, including query parameters.
154    * @throws McpAuthException If the wait times out or is interrupted.
155    */
156   public URI awaitCallback(Duration timeout) {
157      assertArgNotNull("timeout", timeout);
158      try {
159         return callback.get(timeout.toMillis(), TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
160      } catch (TimeoutException e) {
161         throw new McpAuthException("Timed out waiting for the loopback authorization redirect", e);
162      } catch (InterruptedException e) {
163         Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
164         throw new McpAuthException("Interrupted waiting for the loopback authorization redirect", e);
165      } catch (ExecutionException e) { // HTT: callback future is only ever completed normally by the handler
166         throw new McpAuthException("Loopback authorization redirect failed", e); // HTT: only reachable if the future completed exceptionally; see catch line above
167      }
168   }
169
170   @Override /* Overridden from AutoCloseable */
171   public void close() {
172      server.stop(0);
173   }
174}
